newsitem.title: BRAZIL: OLYMPICS-RIO TRIES TO BOLSTER BID WITH HALF A MILLION BALLOONS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-RIO TRIES TO BOLSTER BID WITH HALF A MILLION BALLOONS.

text.p: Half a million latex balloons floated in the skies above Copacabana beach on Sunday in a demonstration of popular support for Rio de Janeiro's bid to host the 2004 Olympics.

The balloons, in the five colours of the Olympic flag, were launched by thousands of local residents who gathered on the world famous beach, most wearing T-shirts with the campaign's "Rio 2004" slogan.

Mortar fire from a yacht anchored off the coast kicked off the ceremony, which also featured ultra-light planes trailing campaign slogans, dances from leading samba schools and a parachuting display over the beach.
The city's social problems and high crime level are seen as stumbling blocks in Rio's bid to host the Olympics.
Rio's organisers have made popular support one of their campaign's trump cards, claiming that 84 percent of the population wants the Games.
"No other candidate city could have put on anything like this," said Ronaldo Cezar Coelho, president of the Rio 2004 committee.
But some environmentalists expressed concerned that launching so many latex balloons set a poor example in terms of environmental education.
